key_insight: For D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr on DSS 2205, increasing spray distance to 190 mm produced the densest coating and the best corrosion resistance in acidic media.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray distance is a simple process lever that can materially improve coating integrity and extend service life of stainless steel components in harsh acid environments.
method: D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr onto DSS 2205 at 170, 180, and 190 mm spray distances.
Characterized surface/microstructure with SEM and porosity measurements.
Evaluated corrosion behavior in 1 M H2SO4 using OCP, EIS, and potentiodynamic polarization.
evidence_signal: The 190 mm coating showed the lowest reported corrosion rate (0.113 mmpy) and porosity dropped from 2.84% at 170 mm to 1.38% at 190 mm.
watch_item: Results are based on a single acidic electrolyte and room-temperature testing, so broader industrial conditions and long-term durability still need validation.
paper_title: Effect of spray distance in D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205 in acidic environments
